title: P1-02 — Persistent owner parent VM, supervisor and SSH
objective: Implement one owner-operated protected persistent parent VM with no default lifetime cap. Approved R1–R10 architecture contract (owner amendments): R1 stable parent_id plus fresh per-boot run_id/host boot ID; R2 one independently verified terminal-independent supervisor and exclusive non-inherited lifecycle lock before children; R3 reuse v3 launch/readiness/exact-identity/ordered-cleanup machinery with explicit smoke-ephemeral versus parent-persistent policy; R4 dry-run recovery and explicit exact-identity signalling only, fail closed on ambiguous spawn/record races; R5 persistent private guest disk/home/config/auth/history/workspace, single writer, explicit image format and path validation; R6 stop and provisioning failure never delete/reset parent state; R7 default bounded guest-disk development workspace, optional explicitly selected validated virtiofs exports; R8 protected pinned OpenCode 2.2.5/session assets (#55); R9 separate per-boot receiver-restricted metrics key and 500-ms push hook in the same supervisor/cleanup (#56); R10 preserve smoke cleanup and add no host authority/child orchestration. Claude architecture review passed with concerns; implementation reviews remain pending. Owner clarification: future capacity increases must be supported through an explicit owner-authorized offline expansion preserving guest data; resize implementation is out of Phase 1 scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: Provide protected project-script up/status/ssh/stop/recover operations for one parent. up is idempotent only after independently verifying matching RUNNING identity; returns success only after bounded readiness. SSH disconnect/OpenCode exit do not stop the VM. Parent uses one terminal-independent supervisor; shared smoke launch/identity/readiness/cleanup primitives are reused, not duplicated.

Parent VM and OpenCode have no default wall-clock cap, idle shutdown, logger byte cap or elapsed-time policy that can terminate a healthy parent. Any optional owner-configured maximum lifetime is disabled by default. Keep smoke timeout and cleanup behavior unchanged.

Stable parent control SSH identity and guest host identity are private and verified for the parent lifetime; each boot has fresh volatile run identity. Owner SSH supports plain shell and reattachable PTY/TUI using the fixed non-forwarding host policy (EscapeChar=none). Remote owner access uses an existing authenticated host SSH/VPN hop; never expose guest SSH publicly or add routes/listeners.

Ordinary stop/up preserves the same protected private guest disk, home, OpenCode configuration, ChatGPT auth, session/conversation history, project files and workspace selection/data. Auth persists across restart until provider expiry/revocation, owner logout/reset, or genuinely new parent. Stop/recovery and provisioning failure never delete or reset persistent state. No host workspace/log/metrics/child-VM credential exposure or unreviewed escrow/backup system.

One independently verifiable supervisor acquires an exclusive private lifecycle lock and records its exact identity and host boot ID before launching children; children cannot inherit lock ownership. stop uses bounded graceful shutdown and existing validated ordered cleanup. recover is dry-run by default, refuses while a live supervisor owns the lock, and only signals independently validated exact identities after explicit owner action. Never PID-only signal, auto-kill a live unresponsive supervisor, infer authority from intent/run tokens, or guess at SIGKILL spawn-before-record or ambiguous orphans; retain evidence and request owner intervention.

Default workspace is guest-disk-backed and persistent on a sparse qcow2 parent disk with configurable creation-time virtual capacity (64 GiB default, not a host-space reservation); distinguish inspectable virtual capacity from actual host allocation and handle host exhaustion safely. Keep disk identity/format/path validated and one-writer enforced. No automatic resize, online resize, shrinking or general disk-management system. Preserve architecture for a future explicit owner-authorized offline expansion, with no resize while running; verify identity, explicit image format and no active writer first. Document a safe offline expansion procedure, including guest partition/filesystem growth, only after the actual guest disk layout is established. Workspace uses normal project read/write/execute semantics, not smoke's 64-MiB noexec bound. No implicit host exports; optional virtiofs requires explicit owner selection and existing canonical-path/ownership/symlink/access validation. Never export broad host dirs, credentials, legacy VM or Docker capabilities; treat guest files as untrusted on host and never auto-source/execute guest hooks/scripts.

Final owner acceptance proves start/status/SSH/stop/reconnect, same-disk/auth/config/history/workspace stop/up persistence, PTY/TUI continuation while live and saved history reopening after reboot, no default timeout, dry-run and controlled explicit recovery, SIGKILL/partial-startup/identity/lock/PID-reuse/boot-ID cases, one-writer/format/path protections, persistent disk retained and smoke disk still deleted, logger limits not terminating healthy parents, and isolation/no host Docker/unapproved access. Runtime checks require owner authorization.

needed: Owner approval for foreground lifecycle/recovery trust boundary and finite deadline.
PTY and resize tests; SIGINT/SIGHUP cleanup; SIGKILL orphan recovery with exact-identity fixtures and host canary.
Full protected smoke on final SHA after any launcher/provisioning change.
Protected script lifecycle start/status/ssh/stop; PTY reconnect and OpenCode exit independence.
No default expiry/idle shutdown; optional max-lifetime policy disabled for parent.
Identity-bound SIGINT/SIGHUP/stop cleanup and owner-only SIGKILL recovery/verification; no PID-file authority.
Per-VM authenticated SSH from owner host and approved remote host-hop, no unapproved forwarding.
Workspace-size/backing review and explicit owner approval before any export expansion.
No runtime testing until owner authorizes the specific host action.

Owner-authorized real-process and owner-VM checks for stop/up preserving the same parent disk, workspace, OpenCode config, auth and session history; verify fresh state only for new parent or explicit owner reset.
Test unlimited-by-default parent lifetime and absence of idle shutdown; supersedes the earlier finite-foreground-deadline planning item. Do not add an optional cap without separately approved policy.

Real-process tests for exclusive private lifecycle locks, no lock inheritance by children, ownership/mode/symlink/path races, host boot ID mismatch, PID reuse, executable/argv mismatch, and ambiguous status.
Exercise SIGKILL between child spawn and identity record; unrecorded children must not be signalled by PID/run token and ambiguous evidence must be retained.
Exercise supervisor SIGKILL with live QEMU/helpers, dry-run recovery, lock conflict with live/unresponsive supervisor, and explicit recovery only for independently validated dead-supervisor children.
Verify explicit image format, single active writer, stable disk identity and guest-disk workspace bound; stop retains parent disk while smoke cleanup still deletes its ephemeral disk.
Verify healthy long-running parent is not terminated by smoke timeout, logger byte cap, or elapsed-time policy; smoke timeout/cap regressions remain unchanged.
Owner-authorized VM test: default guest-disk workspace persists; explicit virtiofs selection is bounded and validated; no implicit host export or host execution of guest files.
Owner-authorized VM test: stop/up preserves auth/config/history without browser login when valid, and OpenCode history can be reopened after reboot.

Verify explicit image format, single active writer, stable disk identity, sparse allocation and 64-GiB configurable creation-time capacity; host usage remains observable, exhaustion fails safely, and no automatic expansion occurs. Stop retains parent disk while smoke cleanup still deletes its ephemeral disk.

Verify explicit image format, single active writer, stable disk identity, sparse allocation, virtual-vs-actual capacity reporting, and safe host-exhaustion behavior. Confirm future offline expansion compatibility and documented layout-specific procedure before owner acceptance; no automatic/online resize, shrink or general disk-management implementation.

S1 implementation review: independently review strict parent-state schemas, read-only status, directory FD protections, disk inode/allocation reporting, and lifecycle flock/noninheritance before parent lifecycle use.

Integrate gated child transition under the live supervisor lock; test supervisor SIGKILL at each spawn/record/release/exec boundary and confirm orphan children are never signalled from PID/token alone.

Before any real parent launch, verify installed QEMU accepts the inherited validated disk FD via -add-fd/fdset with the explicit file→qcow2 block graph, locking=on, correct writable semantics, and no path reopen; test exclusive writer and crash behavior on target filesystem.

Implement and independently review integrated persistent parent provisioning/QEMU/SSH startup and stop; STARTING supervisor scaffold is not a usable VM. Validate QEMU fdset and locking behavior on target runtime before enabling launch. Add identity-bound child lifecycle, readiness, restart/reconnect, recovery dry-run and explicit recovery coverage.

Before enabling parent QEMU launch, verify target QEMU fdset/-add-fd and blockdev options plus exclusive writer lock empirically. Ensure newly created qcow2 has no backing/external data-file metadata and status/provisioning validates explicit format. Validate seed and socat dependency behavior. Do not treat argv tests or source documentation review as runtime evidence.

Before exposing provisioning via CLI or connecting it to `up`, close same-UID pathname races in qemu-img output creation/publication (or explicitly document the trust boundary) and add tool/runtime validation on the intended host. Do not infer sparse qcow2 semantics from mocked tiny fixture.
